current_conclusion: Micromorphic coupling is the only change tested that measurably brings the reconstruction closer to DIC: under symmetric image-level observation it improves relative L2 by 9.6 times the metric's noise margin and correlation by 3.2 times, and it brings the over-active q90 area from +61 % down to +2.6 % of the DIC reference. It does so while degrading where the localisation sits, by 2.4 and 2.5 margins on the two overlap measures, so the ranking depends on the objective and neither Hchi nor ell is identified. By contrast the measured 40-state loading path, which now replays end to end after a defect in the elastic predictor was fixed, changes core PEEQ by 15.8 % yet moves no DIC metric beyond its margin. A fast SRIX equilibrium-gap surrogate recovers and ranks exact digital twins, but its ranking fails after the qualified DIC transfer, so SRIX parameter identification on P43 is currently blocked. The local and coupled mechanics are numerically verified; no transferable material internal length is claimed.
